More than a hundred civil society organizations, including Human Rights Watch, have called on Egyptian authorities to end the prosecution of Attalah and grant Mada Masr a license to operate. Attalah’s prosecution comes amid a broader crackdown on independent media in Egypt and less than a month after security forces arrested six journalists working for the independent investigative journalism platform Matsda2sh on September 28 and 29, 2026. The journalists, who constituted the platform’s entire editorial newsroom, remain in pretrial detention facing charges of “joining and financing a terrorist group,” “spreading false news,” and using social media to disseminate it. Some of them have since alleged that the authorities tortured them in detention and attempted to extract coerced confessions, according to their lawyers. The authorities should drop all charges stemming from exercising the right to freedom of expression and end their repeated harassment of independent media, Human Rights Watch said. Egypt remains one of the world’s leading jailers of journalists, with 25 journalists behind bars as of early October, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists. Egyptian authorities have blocked access to Mada Masr’s website in Egypt since May 2017. Egypt is obligated under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights to respect freedom of expression, including press freedom. The United Nations Human Rights Committee, which authoritatively interprets the covenant, has found that governments may not prohibit a site or an information dissemination system from publishing material solely on the basis that it may be critical of the government. “Setting registration requirements and then repeatedly ignoring Mada Masr’s good faith attempts to fulfill them is a transparent attempt by authorities to undermine the platform and violates international human rights law,” Khawaja said. “The Egyptian authorities should drop the charges and end the ongoing crackdown on independent journalism.”

Azerbaijan’s Hijab Restrictions Exclude Girls From School. Click to expand Image Three Azerbaijani women wearing headscarves in Baku, Azerbaijan. © 2019 Getty Images School officials across Azerbaijan have been turning away girls wearing hijabs following the introduction of new government dress regulations, sparking protests across the country. Police have detained dozens of people amid the protests, while Instagram and TikTok users have reported difficulties accessing the platforms as public criticism of the restrictions has grown. Azerbaijan’s Cabinet of Ministers amended school uniform regulations on September 21, prohibiting clothing "inconsistent with the principle of secular education." Although the regulations do not explicitly mention hijabs, schools began refusing entry to girls wearing headscarfs when the rules took effect on October 12. News reports showed distressed girls after being turned away from schools. Separate dress requirements adopted on October 6 also affected teachers. Authorities responded to the protests with widespread detentions. The Ministry of Interior acknowledged on October 12 that they had detained 37 people in Baku, alleging disruptions to public order. Independent media reported that more than 200 people were detained near a central Baku metro station that evening. Activists also reported 88 detentions in Nardaran village, with criminal cases opened against many of those detained. People criticizing the restrictions online have also faced detention. Unidentified individuals reportedly took activist İlkin Hüseynov from his home on October 14, a day after he launched "Let Leyli Go to School," an online initiative connecting volunteer teachers with girls excluded from classrooms. He was subsequently sentenced to 30 days detention for allegedly disobeying police orders. In Nakhchivan, a man reportedly received a sentence for 25 days detention following a TikTok post about the restrictions. Social media users across Azerbaijan also reported difficulties accessing Instagram and TikTok on October 12; some were only able to connect via virtual private networks. Excluding girls from schools because they wear religious headscarves interferes with their rights to education and freedom of religion or belief, and raises serious concerns about discrimination. While governments may regulate school attire, any restrictions must be lawful, necessary, proportionate and non-discriminatory. Azerbaijan should not use the principle of secular education to deny girls access to schooling. Azerbaijani authorities should immediately ensure that students and teachers wearing hijabs can attend schools, release anyone detained solely for peacefully protesting or criticizing the restrictions, ensure access to legal counsel for those in custody, and investigate reports of interference with social media access.

Egypt: Prominent Journalist Lina Attalah Detained. Click to expand Image Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of Mada Masr, in Cairo, Egypt, November 24, 2017. © 2017 Roger Anis/AP Photo (Beirut) - The New Cairo Misdemeanor Court convicted Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent news platform Mada Masr, of operating without a license in a single hearing on October 27, 2026. The court fined her 3 million Egyptian pounds (US$53,474) and ordered the website’s closure. The authorities took Attalah into custody after the hearing. Mada Masr reported that prior to ruling, the judge cleared the courtroom, rejected all procedural motions presented by Attalah’s defense team including requests to present evidence and hear from witnesses, and replaced her defense counsel against her will. Attalah had received a summons on October 19 to appear for questioning before the Supreme State Security Prosecution and Egyptian authorities on October 22 referred her to trial on charges of establishing, managing, and operating a website without a license. The following quote can be attributed to Bassam Khawaja, deputy Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch: “The summary conviction of Lina Attalah in a sham process involving a single, rushed hearing is a complete travesty of justice. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s government is clearly determined to wipe out the last remnants of independent media in the country. Egypt’s international partners should loudly condemn this outrageous crackdown.”

Syria's New Reconstruction Fund a Chance for Reform. Click to expand Image An aerial view of a damaged area of Damascus where the debris from collapsed buildings is being turned into sand, gravel, and bricks to reuse as construction materials to restore areas affected by Syria’s civil war, November 2, 2025. © 2025 Bakr Al Kasem/Anadolu via Getty Images Syria and the World Bank Group announced on October 18 the creation of the Syria Recovery and Reconstruction Trust Fund, known as START. Run by the World Bank, the fund will pool donor money and private investment to help restore infrastructure and public services, strengthen state institutions, and finance reforms the Syrian government identifies as priorities. The World Bank estimates Syria’s post-conflict reconstruction will cost about US$216 billion. Norway pledged approximately 90 million krone ($9.6 million) and the Netherlands €15 million ($16.8 million). START’s initial focus, according to Syria’s state news agency, SANA, is infrastructure, health and education. It will operate under World Bank policies, which include standards on stakeholder engagement, land acquisition, and grievance mechanisms. But those standards only cover START-funded projects and governance arrangements are still being finalized, according to SANA. The moment offers a chance to strengthen protections for Syria’s wider reconstruction, beyond START’s projects. Current rules governing reconstruction do not require consultation with affected communities, including tenants, informal occupants, and displaced people before projects are approved, and there is no specialized mechanism for reconstruction disputes. The consequences of policies that are implemented without consulting those most affected are already evident: In March, local authorities in Damascus proposed giving foreign companies land in Jobar and Qaboun in exchange for financing and building a reconstruction project. Owners of homes in zoned areas would get new units half the size of their old ones. Owners of land in informal settlements would get only 30 percent of their land. And the plan made no provision for tenants. The World Bank and START's donors should make a rights-aligned framework for housing, land, and property a priority among the reforms the fund supports, including an independent property dispute mechanism. They should require human rights impact assessments before funding projects with unresolved property claims. They should prioritize restoring services where people are returning. And any support for private health or education providers should carry enforceable requirements on affordability, quality, and nondiscrimination. Finance Minister Yisr Barnieh says the priority now is “tangible results for the Syrian people.” The real test is whether those people have a say in decisions about their land and whether they can enjoy their rights to health, education, and housing.

Brazil: New Evidence of Serious Police Misconduct in Deadly Raid. Play Video Read a text description of this video TEXT ON SCREEN October 28, 2025 Rio de Janeiro, Brazil NARRATION On the morning of October 28th, 2025, hundreds of police officers surrounded two low-income neighborhoods in Rio de Janeiro. By nightfall, the operation would become the deadliest in Brazil's history. TEXT ON SCREEN WARNING. This video contains graphic content, including blurred images of dead bodies. Viewer discretion advised. NARRATION 122 people were killed, including two children and five police officers. According to the autopsy records, over eighty five percent of non-police victims were Black. Police in Rio de Janeiro are required by Supreme Court order to wear body cameras. However, only twenty-three percent of officers wore body cameras that day, and in the footage reviewed by Human Rights Watch, not a single killing was captured on camera. LOWER THIRD Damir Khairat Research Technologist Digital Investigations Lab NARRATION Human Rights Watch was given access to the prosecutor's investigation into the operation, including 8,800 pages of records, 122 autopsies, and nearly 4,000 hours of body camera footage. TEXT ON SCREEN Prosecutors have released the body camera footage shown in this video. Most footage is sealed as evidence and cannot be published. NARRATION Watching all the footage day and night without any breaks would have taken a single researcher almost six months. So, we trained several artificial intelligence models to help us identify the moments that mattered most. First, we needed to organize everything. The models, alongside software that Human Rights Watch developed, synchronized recordings from different officers, mapped their locations, and scanned footage for gunshots and signs of camera tampering. From there we had a searchable platform that let us view the operation as one coordinated event, rather than thousands of separate recordings. What we found was evidence of widespread tampering and obstruction of body cameras. And it consistently happened at the exact moment cameras should have been recording, during arrests, shootouts, or while officers entered homes. Authorities said that the purpose of the raid was to arrest suspected drug traffickers. The evidence we found points to an operation that appeared lethal by design. To explain how we came to this conclusion, let's look at some examples of the moments we trained our AI models to detect. An officer's camera captured this video in an alleyway as a large group of his colleagues pass by, after which the officer quickly covers his camera. He or another officer then flags that there's a camera recording. SOUNDBITE [IN PORTUGUESE] The team has a camera. The team has a camera. No, no I’m talking about the thing there. NARRATION It's unclear why he covered it, but prosecutors later charged him with camera tampering. SOUNDBITE So, this would be the kind of like overall operational view. NARRATION To find incidents like this across almost 4,000 hours of footage from nearly 500 officers, we trained a model to detect similar moments when a camera continued recording, but the lens was covered. Here, an officer is seen struggling to pick the lock on the door of someone's home. Once it's open, he removes his camera and leaves it unattended for over an hour, presumably while he's inside the home. Because the camera was still capturing an image, this recording wasn't initially flagged by our software. So, we trained a second model to identify "stale scenes" where the recording stays the same for long periods of time. As our models learned and improved, they uncovered lots of suspicious recording gaps. In the end, we documented more than 250 camera obstructions. Moments like these are exactly the situations that body cameras are meant to document, helping ensure that any unlawful behavior is captured and that circumstances surrounding the 122 killings can be properly investigated. Another method we used was an AI system that analyzes audio to detect gunshots. After we trained it specifically for Rio police body cameras and local conditions, the model successfully detected most gunshots in a test set of videos. We were also able to use AI to pull text directly from the videos, like the date, time, location and ID number of the officer wearing the camera. But one of the most striking findings came from what we didn't see. Despite the scale of the operation and the number of deaths, we found no footage showing the killings themselves. NARRATION To understand what was missing, we organized body camera recordings across the operation using extracted timestamps. TEXT ON SCREEN Unusable footage Usable footage NARRATION We found that more than half the officers’ recordings had either ended or had significant gaps by noon. From there, the usable footage continued to decline, just as the operation became most deadly. The missing footage, combined with extensive evidence of camera tampering, suggests that body cameras were deliberately misused to prevent killings from being recorded. Throughout our investigation, AI was one tool out of many. Our team of researchers interviewed witnesses in Rio, visited the neighborhood where the killings took place, analyzed police records and autopsies, verified photographs and videos, and manually reviewed AI findings. What AI provided was speed and scale. It helped us process thousands of hours of footage, connect pieces of evidence, and focus our attention where it mattered most. In other words, AI helped us find needles in a very large haystack. Now, it's up to Brazilian prosecutors to thoroughly investigate both the killings and the decisions that led to such a deadly operation. Those who use disproportionate force or misuse body cameras should be held accountable. To learn more about the events of October 28th and Human Rights Watch’s findings, visit HRW.org and read our investigation, A Strategy of Death. Police officers tampered with body cameras and was responsible for serious investigative failures during an operation ostensibly to arrest gang members in a low-income neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro on October 28, 2025. A year-long Human Rights Watch investigation concluded that police breached Supreme Court orders and their own protocols during Operation Containment, which appeared to be lethal by design. Federal and state prosecutors should initiate criminal and civil proceedings to investigate those responsible for abuses, including senior officials and police commanders. (Rio de Janeiro, October 28, 2026) – Police officers tampered with body cameras and failed to take crucial investigative steps during an operation in a low-income neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on October 28, 2025, Human Rights Watch said in an investigation published today. Evidence indicates police used excessive force and may have intentionally killed scores of men and boys. The investigation, “‘A Strategy of Death’: Investigating Brazil’s Deadliest Police Operation,” documents Operation Containment (Operação Contenção), in which a total of 122 people were killed. This included two children and four police officers killed that day, and a fifth police officer who later succumbed to his wounds. An additional two men were killed in the early morning before the official start of the operation. Eighty-five percent of non-police victims of the October 2025 raid were Black. “A Strategy of Death” Investigating Brazil’s Deadliest Police Operation Read the full investigation here None of the killings were captured in the thousands of hours of body camera footage sent by Rio de Janeiro Military Police to the Public Defender’s Office, which Human Rights Watch reviewed after being granted access. “Human Rights Watch processed thousands of hours of body camera footage and analyzed videos, official investigation files, and autopsy records for every victim, yet crucial questions remain because police failed to properly record killings, preserve crime scenes, or collect crucial data,” said Sophia Jones, open source researcher with the Digital Investigations Lab at Human Rights Watch. “The families of those killed, including police officers, deserve answers and accountability with a thorough, independent investigation.” Human Rights Watch interviewed 41 witnesses, family members, and experts, and analyzed 4,400 hours of body camera footage, 9,000 pages of official investigation files, 122 autopsy reports, court records, and hundreds of videos and photographs. Human Rights Watch analyzed the data using several machine learning models built in-house, followed by manual review and assessment by researchers. Based on Human Rights Watch analysis of data from Rio-based security research lab GENI (Grupo de Estudos dos Novos Ilegalismos or Group for the Study of New Illegalities), nongovernmental think tank Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública (Brazilian Public Security Forum), independent security monitoring organization Fogo Cruzado (Crossfire), and media reports, Operation Containment was the deadliest documented one-day police operation in a country where police forces kill more than 6,000 people per year. Human Rights Watch visited the Complexo da Penha, the site of the operation, six months after the raid and found that the criminal group Red Command (Comando Vermelho)—the target of the operation—continued to impose its rule on residents. Despite the stated goal of carrying out 100 arrest warrants for alleged Red Command members, police records show they arrested only 17 of those for whom they had warrants, although it is not clear whether those are the warrants that justified the operation or other pending warrants. Police did not enter the home of the local Red Command leader, for whom they had a warrant, a Civil Police commander told prosecutors, even though body camera footage shows police moving around it. Despite a state law and a Supreme Court order mandating that police wear body cameras, only about 23 percent of the 2,500 civil and military police officers who participated in the raid did, the Rio de Janeiro government said. Machine-Enabled Forensics How Human Rights Watch used Artificial Intelligence to Analyze Body Camera Footage from Rio’s Deadliest Police Raid Read the methodology here Human Rights Watch analysis of the footage of the 527 military police officers who wore the cameras found widespread tampering and obstruction of their use. Officers left cameras running before the operation, effectively draining batteries; covered lenses; placed cameras where they would not capture officers’ actions; and left cameras in vehicles. Such tampering consistently occurred at key moments, during arrests, shootouts, or while officers entered homes, researchers found. Most tampering was on cameras worn by officers whose units engaged in frontline operations, such as the Battalion of Special Police Operations of the Military Police, the unit deployed to the forested area where the majority of killings took place. Researchers determined that 36 percent of gunshot clusters heard on their cameras occurred when the cameras were obstructed. Body camera footage showed officers assaulting and threatening to kill detainees, including a child, whom they forced to lie down next to a dead body while photographing him. In another recording, an officer tells officers to shoot detainees in the legs if they ran. In a third clip, an officer expressed frustration that body cameras prevented them from killing suspects. Researchers also analyzed or verified hundreds of videos and photographs taken by members of the local community that day. In one series of verified videos, officers pile dead bodies, some with their genitalia exposed, into an armored police vehicle, while joking. “Look how wonderful,” one officer said. “We like this.” While police said they spent months planning the operation, there was no evidence that they made any advance preparations to protect crime scenes and conduct forensic analysis. In addition, Civil Police failed to collect basic information for all but two of the 117 non-police victims, such as the names of police officers and residents who brought some of them to a hospital. Only seven suspects were taken to a hospital and subsequently arrested, compared with 117 people killed by police. That unusually high ratio of people killed to people injured (17 to 1) raises serious questions about whether police prioritized lethal force over arresting suspects. An analysis of victim autopsy reports also points in that direction. Over 40 percent of non-police victims in the reports analyzed were shot in the head, over 60 percent were shot four or more times, and nearly 75 percent were shot at least once on the back. One man was shot and then decapitated. According to forensic experts from the Independent Forensic Expert Group of the International Rehabilitation Council for Torture Victims consulted by Human Rights Watch, the evidence suggests that many were targeted and killed intentionally. In many instances, the trajectory of gunshot wounds was from bottom to top, which can be indicative of execution, such as when an individual is shot while lying down or otherwise incapacitated. Brazilian authorities should ensure a thorough and independent investigation into the planning and decisions by senior officials and police commanders that led to the deadly operation. Rio de Janeiro’s new governor, who will take office on January 6, 2027, should introduce a bill to separate forensic services from the Civil Police. “Our investigation shows police flouted the law and their own protocols during the disastrous raid,” said César Muñoz, Brazil director at Human Rights Watch. “Abusive police practices undermine public security by making communities less willing to collaborate with police, while fueling a cycle of violence that endangers both residents and police officers. Brazil needs new effective public security strategies that uphold human rights.”

La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

TERRORE IN ASPROMONTE:AVVISTATI OMINI VERDI. Sono tante le domande in merito: si è trattato di extraterrestri? Di una qualche antica razza di ominidi ) sfuggita all’evoluzione? Di esperimenti eugenetici che si svolgono nei sotterranei della base ex-Usaf di Nardello ? Di uno Stargate nascosto tra le rocce di Pietra Cappa? Sta di fatto che il triangolo, tra Solano, Roccaforte del Greco e Caraffa è stato troppo spesso teatro d’inspiegabili fenomeni. Proprio circa un anno fa si è verificato un episodio che ha sconvolto l’intero Aspromonte . È stato avvisato, da un affermato cercatore di funghi, un mostro senza braccia, con due gambe di cavallo e la barba lunghissima . Il mostro – ha assicurato il tizio sotto shock – scorrazzava per i monti con fare minaccioso azzannando tutto ciò che si muoveva. Qualcuno ha avanzato l’ipotesi che possa essersi trattato di un animale soggetto a malformazioni dovute a qualche forte fonte di radiazioni, probabilmente emesse dalle antenne della Base militare di Nardello. Altri hanno ipotizzato che si è trattato di uno scherzo o di un’allucinazione causata da qualche fungo con proprietà allucinogene. Questo ci ha spinto, però, ad avviare un’indagine con tanto di sopralluogo nel perimetro interessato. Quello che abbiamo scoperto ha dell’incredibile! Non poche sono state infatti le persone (soggetti attendibilissimi) che (mettendo da parte la storia del mostro) hanno dichiarato di essersi imbattuti, nel corso degli anni e durante i periodi dei lavori di campagna, con dei piccoli omini verdi. Esseri buffi – secondo loro – non più alti del metro e venti, piuttosto schivi, che si aggirano furtivamente per le campagne di Stole, ma anche di Varet e di Campolaco. Come detto, sono molte le testimonianze in tal senso. BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.

Djokovic celebra la vittoria degli studenti in Serbia: "Sono molto felice". Novak Djokovic si dice molto felice che gli studenti abbiano sconfitto Vučić alle elezioni in Serbia. «Sono molto felice di tutto questo. Il mio più profondo rispetto va agli studenti, che hanno lottato dimostrando dignità e resilienza. Provo una grande ammirazione per ciò che hanno fatto. Sono riusciti a far nascere un senso di orgoglio per la Serbia, sia nel Paese sia nel resto del mondo. La vittoria è ormai assicurata e tutti noi nutriamo la speranza che il nostro Paese possa prosperare e godersi il futuro che ci attende». Novak Djokovic, in passato in contatto stretto con l'ormai ex presidente serbo Aleksandar Vucic, quasi amico intimo, l'anno scorso ha portato via il suo torneo Belgrado Open, spostandolo dalla capitale serba alla Grecia, in opposizione all'ex leader. Un dissenso maturato negli ultimi anni, proprio in concomitanza con il nascere delle proteste studentesche di piazza contro un regime definito anti-democratico e contro la corruzione. Roma, blitz contro la mostra di Laika: immobilizzano il gallerista e imbrattano le opere. Tre persone incappucciate hanno fatto irruzione nella galleria Rosso20sette di Roma, imbrattando con vernice nera le opere esposte della street artist Laika. L'episodio è avvenuto nel tardo pomeriggio del 27 ottobre, mentre all'interno dello spazio espositivo si trovava soltanto il gallerista Stefano Ferraro, che, secondo le prime ricostruzioni, è stato minacciato e immobilizzato dagli aggressori. La mostra, intitolata The Collapse of Democracy – States of Injustice, Chapter 2, raccoglie una ventina di lavori tra tele, opere su carta e installazioni realizzati dopo il secondo viaggio dell'artista negli Stati Uniti. Tra i soggetti rappresentati ci sono Donald Trump raffigurato nudo, una Tesla in fiamme, Patti Smith con la scritta «Free Palestine» e figure simbolo della lotta al razzismo come Rosa Parks e Martin Luther King. La galleria non dispone di telecamere di sorveglianza interne, ma alcuni dispositivi sono presenti nella strada. Laika aveva già ricevuto minacce sui social, ma il movente dell'irruzione non è stato accertato.
